title: State Pattern
overview: Allow an object to alter its behaviour when its internal state changes, appearing to change its class.
useCases: An object's behaviour varies based on its current state, and you want to eliminate large conditional statements and make state transitions easier to manage
You want each state's logic to live in its own class rather than scattered across if/switch blocks
Modelling workflows or lifecycles where an entity moves through well-defined states (e.g. order: pending → paid → shipped → delivered)
exampleUses: A vending machine that behaves differently (accept coins, dispense item, return change) depending on whether it is idle, has credit, or is dispensing
A TCP connection object whose open(), close(), and acknowledge() methods behave differently based on the current connection state (Established, Listen, Closed)
A document editor where the toolbar responds differently to clicks depending on whether the document is in view, edit, or review mode
